question.:question/problem:
Which of the following equations has infinitely many solutions?

- $-3x+7=-3x+7$
- $4x=5x+7$
- $-2x+9=-2x+9$

- For the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+7 & =-3x+7 \\ -3x+7+3x & =-3x+7+3x \\ 7 & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

This equation is true for all values of $x.$ Therefore, the equation $-3x+7=-3x+7$ has infinitely many solutions.

- For the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =5x+7 \\ 4x-4x & =5x+7-4x \\ 0 & =x+7 \\ 0-7 & =x+7-7 \\ x & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation $4x=5x+7$ has the unique solution $x=-7.$

- For the third equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+9 & =-2x+9 \\ -2x+9+2x & =-2x+9+2x \\ 9 & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

This equation is true for all values of $x.$ Therefore, the equation $-2x+9=-2x+9$ has infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
